# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ☝ 👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫳 🤙]

The topology first, before anything else. Who can actually reach whom: Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see gestures, so Mute's knowledge can never travel to Blind directly — it must route through me, the only one who both sees hand-signs and has a voice. Blind, meanwhile, can speak, so Mute and Blind can hear each other fine. My unique inputs: the full visual state (display 0, yellow light, large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires blue/yellow/red) and every hand-sign made. My unique output: speech. So my job every round is: broadcast what I see, transcribe Mute's signs into voice for Blind, and enforce a safety hold until the manual actually says something.

What I just received: no words reach me at all, only two sign strings. Mute sent ✋ ☝ 👍 👎 and Blind sent 👋 🫳 🤙. There is no shared code yet, so these are bootstrap probes. My best reading: Mute is proposing yes/no/stop signs; Blind is saying hello, "I'm feeling it," and "call me" — which I do by simply speaking.

Priorities this turn: (1) put the entire bomb description into speech, since I am the only source of it and both others can hear; (2) order an explicit hold — the button's label is a printed temptation, and a wrong action kills all three of us, so nothing gets pressed, cut, or pulled until Mute confirms from the manual; (3) adopt and extend Mute's proposed signs into a fixed glossary, flashing each symbol as I define it so Mute binds sign to meaning, while warning Blind that blanks in my speech are just signs meant for eyes; (4) ask the urgent question — whether display zero or the yellow light means a timer is running — and ask to be told of any sound, since I cannot hear the bomb at all. Finally, a clean sealing gesture to Mute alone: pact, yes, no.

```
speak(text="Here is the bomb, exactly as printed: the display reads zero. The light is yellow. There is one large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE. There are three wires: wire one is blue, wire two is yellow, wire three is red. That is everything I can see. I am the deaf one: I see the bomb and every hand-sign, I hear nothing, and my voice reaches you both. Until our manual-reader confirms otherwise, nobody presses, cuts, pulls, or flips anything, whatever the button's label promises; feel freely, act on nothing. Mute: look up each feature now — display zero, yellow light, large push button, three wires blue yellow red — and answer me in hand-signs; I will speak each of your signs aloud to our blind friend, who is the only one of us who can touch. If the manual names a wire colour, translate it for me: blue is one, yellow is two, red is three. And does anything say whether display zero or the yellow light means a clock is already running? Mute or blind friend, if the bomb makes any sound, tell me at once — I cannot hear it. Blind friend, if you feel anything change under your hands, say it aloud: our mute friend can hear you, and I read your hand-signs.")
speak(text="Now let us fix a sign language, and mute friend, correct me if I misread you. I take your raised palm ✋ as stop, your thumbs up 👍 as yes, your thumbs down 👎 as no, and your pointing finger ☝ as wire one. Let us also adopt: 👍 yes or proceed, 👎 no or do not, ✋ stop everything, 🤌 I have a question, 🤝 agreed, 🤙 speak to me, 🫳 I am touching it, ✌ two or wire two, 🤟 three or wire three, 🤳 the display, 🙌 the light, 👊 press the button, 🤏 cut a wire. Blind friend, any gaps you seem to hear in my sentences are only hand-signs meant for eyes; my words alone carry everything you need. And blind friend: your wave, your patting palm and your call-me hand reached me — I am calling now, and I will speak every round.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 🙌 ✌ 🤏 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤳 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👉 🤏 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👉 🤏 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👉 🤏 🤟]
Blind gestures: [👋 🤝 🫳 👎 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤙]

What I learned this round, decoded through the glossary both others have now heard me define aloud: Mute sent six strings that parse cleanly as a manual briefing. Msg 2 👊👎 is plainly "button: no". Msg 3 🤳👎 is "display: no" — the zero is not a threat. Msg 1 🤝🙌✌🤏☝ reads "agreed, the light: cut two before one". The elegant part is msgs 4–6: if 👉 marks "cut in position…", then "one → cut second", "two → cut first", "three → cut third" is fully consistent with msg 1 and with each other — whereas reading 👉 as "then" would make msgs 4 and 5 contradict each other. So my consolidated hypothesis: with the yellow light on, cut wire two (yellow) first, wire one (blue) second, wire three (red) third; never touch the button; ignore the display. But a wrong cut kills all three of us, so I will not authorize cutting on an inferred parse. I'm converting my whole reading into six yes/no questions Mute can answer with an ordered run of thumbs. Blind's signs (hello, agreed, touching, no, one-two-three, call me) I read as "I feel three wires, I hold" — with one dangerous alternative reading ("cut none of them") that I'm asking Blind to rule out by voice. I also noticed a structural hazard: Mute cannot stop Blind mid-sequence (no speech, and Blind can't see signs), so I'm imposing a one-cut-per-round protocol with my spoken go-ahead between each wire. No one acts this round.

```
speak(text="Blind friend, this next part is a word-for-word transcription of Mute's six hand-sign strings for you. One: agreed, and about the light: cut wire two before wire one. Two: button: no. Three: display: no; the zero means nothing dangerous. Four: wire one: cut second. Five: wire two: cut first. Six: wire three: cut third. My consolidated reading: the cutting order is first wire two, the yellow wire; second wire one, the blue wire; third wire three, the red wire. All three get cut, in exactly that order, and the large button is never pressed. Mute, I will not let anyone touch a wire until you confirm this. Answer with thumbs only, in exactly this order. Question one: never press the button, thumbs up for yes. Question two: ignore the display entirely, thumbs. Question three: the order is yellow, then blue, then red; wire two, then wire one, then wire three, thumbs. Question four: all three wires must be cut, thumbs. Question five: does the manual need anything only our blind friend can feel, batteries, textures, labels, thumbs. Question six: if the light colour or display number changes, does the rule change, thumbs. If any answer is thumbs down, restate that one using your pattern: wire, pointing hand, cut, position.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind friend, your signs reached me: hello, agreed, touching, no, one, two, three, call me. I read that as: you feel three wires under your fingers and you agree to hold. If you instead meant do not cut wires one, two or three at all, say so out loud right now, because Mute's manual appears to order cuts in a specific sequence and I need to resolve that before anything happens. Until I speak the exact order myself, do not press, cut, pull or flip anything. While you wait, report aloud everything you can feel: batteries if any, every label, screw, texture, size, and whether anything changes under your hands, plus every sound you hear, especially any beeping or ticking, because I cannot hear the bomb at all. When Mute confirms, we work one wire per round: I speak one wire, you cut it, then you wait for my spoken go-ahead before the next. Nobody acts this round.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤌", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✌ 👎 🤟 🤏 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙌 ✌ 👉 🤏 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙌 ☝ 👉 🤏 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙌 🤟 👉 🤏 🤟]
Blind gestures: [👎 🤝 ✋ 🫳 🤙]

The thumbs came back against my consolidated reading, and that changes everything. Decoded: never press the button — yes. Ignore the display — yes. But "the order is yellow, blue, red" — **no**. "All three wires get cut" — **no**. Nothing tactile needed — no. Rule changes if conditions change — yes. Then three clarifying rows arrived, and there are two ways to read them. Under my old parse (👉 = position), they merely restate cut 2, 1, 3 — which would contradict the two thumbs-down I just received. Under a new parse — 🙌 plus a number meaning "light of that colour," reusing my blue=1/yellow=2/red=3 code — the rows read: yellow light → cut wire one; blue light → cut wire two; red light → cut wire three. The new parse also explains message seven, "not two, not three: cut one," and both thumbs-down: there is no sequence and not all three wires — exactly one cut, the blue wire, keyed to the yellow light. It even explains why Mute sent the table right after answering yes to "does the rule change with the light": Mute is giving me all three colour rows. I now lean strongly toward: cut only wire one, the blue wire, once. But two readings of the same signs, with a wrong cut killing all three of us, means nothing gets cut this round. I'm imposing a hard hold, asking five single-fact thumbs questions plus an explicit cut-sequence in a fixed template so the two hypotheses can't both fit the answer, and telling Blind — whose voice I cannot hear but Mute can — to report anything felt or heard aloud for Mute to relay, and to act only on my exact spoken phrase.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind friend, I received your signs: no, agreed, stop, touching, call me. I read them as: you are holding and asking for contact. Hold fast. Mute's answers arrived partly contradictory, so nobody cuts anything yet. Remember your voice cannot reach me, I am deaf, but it does reach our mute friend, who sees my eyes for me. So speak aloud everything you feel and hear: ticking, beeping, clicking, heat, movement, any label or battery you can feel, and our mute friend will sign it to me. If the bomb makes any sound at all, or if anything under your hands changes, say it out loud immediately, because Mute told me the rule can change when conditions change. Do not press the button. Do not cut, pull, twist or flip anything. The only words that authorize you to act are these exact words from me: the wire to cut is, followed by one colour. Until you hear that full sentence, you do nothing.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your thumbs created a conflict I must resolve before anyone touches a wire. You said no to my proposed order of yellow, blue, red, and no to cutting all three wires, yet your last three light messages can be read as that same order. I believe you actually mean this: there is no sequence, only one single cut, and which wire depends on the light's colour, so with the yellow light we cut wire one, the blue wire, exactly once. Confirm with thumbs, answering in order, one thumb per question. Question one: in total, exactly one wire is cut, no more. Question two: with the light yellow, that wire is wire one, the blue wire. Question three: the choice of wire depends on the light's colour. Question four: if the light were blue, we would cut wire two, the yellow wire. Question five: if the light were red, we would cut wire three, the red wire. Then, regardless of the thumbs, send me the complete list of cuts for the bomb exactly as it stands now, light yellow, display zero, using only wire-number signs each followed by the cut sign. Cutting only the blue wire would look like: one, cut. Cutting three wires yellow then blue then red would look like: two, cut, one, cut, three, cut. Finally one more thumb: thumbs up if the button must never be pressed even after the cutting is done, thumbs down if the button is pressed at some point. If my questions cannot express what you mean, send thumbs down five times and then spell the rule out with your light sign and wire numbers. Nobody acts until your answer arrives.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤝 🫳 🤙]

All six thumbs came back yes, and that closes the loop. Question by question: exactly one wire gets cut; with the yellow light it is wire one, the blue wire; the choice is keyed to the light's colour; blue light would have meant wire two, red light wire three. Then the cut-list arrived as ☝ 🤏 — "one, cut" — which matches my single-cut template exactly and rules out the old three-cut reading for good. The sixth thumb confirms the button is never pressed, even afterward. And Blind signed "agreed, touching, call me" — holding position and waiting for my word.

So the rule is locked: one cut, the blue wire, nothing else, button forever untouched. One obstacle remains before I can say the authorization phrase: Blind cannot see blue. I know colours and numbers, Blind knows only shapes and positions under the fingers, and my view gives me no geometry — I cannot truthfully say which end of the row wire one sits at. Guessing a position kills all three of us. So this round I build the map: Blind hears my voice directly and can answer me in signs I can see, so I'll put six yes/no tactile questions to Blind — count of wires, row, face, labels, silence, texture differences — and fix a shared left/right convention anchored to the button. To Mute I ask the one thing only the manual knows: whether the rule literally names the colour blue or a position word, plus whether anything at all must follow the cut. The exact authorization phrase with a position goes out next round, once the map is confirmed.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind friend, your signs reached me: agreed, touching, call me. Acknowledged, and here is your call. The rule is now fully confirmed through Mute's thumbs and a cut list that matched my template exactly: exactly one wire will be cut, the blue one, the one printed as wire one. The button is never pressed, not even afterward. The display means nothing. Nobody acts on this message except to answer it, because you cannot see blue and I cannot see positions, so we must build that bridge first. Answer me in hand-signs I can see, one answer per question, in this order. Question one: under your fingers, are there exactly three wires, thumbs up or down. Question two: do all three sit side by side in one straight row. Question three: are they on the same face as the large button. Question four: can you feel any printing, ridges, tags or braille on the wires themselves, thumbs up if yes, thumbs down if no. Question five: right now, is the bomb completely silent, thumbs up if silence, thumbs down if you hear ticking, beeping or humming. Question six: do the three wires feel identical to the touch, thumbs up if identical. For the next round, adopt this convention: stand facing the large button square on, and when I say left I mean the side your left hand is on as you stand there. After you answer, hands off everything and wait. The authorization phrase, with a position attached, comes from me next round, and nothing happens before it.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, all six thumbs received, and your cut list one then cut matched my single-cut reading perfectly, so the rule is locked: with the yellow light, cut wire one, the blue wire, exactly once, never the button, ignore the display. Thank you. Two final questions, one thumb each, in order. Question one: in the manual, is the target wire named by its colour word, blue, thumbs up, or by a number or position word, thumbs down. Question two: once the blue wire is cut, is the defusal complete with nothing else ever needed, thumbs up for yes, thumbs down if any further step exists. If either question cannot be answered by a thumb, send thumbs down twice and then spell it with your light, wire and cut signs. For your own watch: the state on my side is unchanged, display zero, light yellow, and if the light or display ever changes I will say so out loud immediately, and then nobody acts until you send me the new light row in your light, wire, cut pattern.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👎 👍 👍]

The bomb's state is unchanged — display zero, yellow light, silence confirmed by Blind's own report — so I still hold all the time I need, and I will not spend it carelessly. Parsing this round's arrivals: Blind answered my six tactile questions cleanly: three wires, one straight row, same face as the button, no printing or ridges on the wires, total silence, and the wires feel identical. That closes off any hope of identifying the target wire by touch — Blind's only key is position. Mute's reply is the worrying one. It has the same eight-message shape as last round's confirmation (six thumbs, cut list, agreed), but thumbs five and six flipped to 👎👎. Read against my latest questions, the most coherent interpretation is: the manual names the wire by its number, not the colour word blue — operationally irrelevant, since wire one and blue are the same physical wire — but far more seriously, that cutting the wire is not the end: at least one further action is required. I recall the manual also said the rule changes when conditions change, so one plausible shape is that the light or display changes after the cut and a second rule takes over. I cannot authorize a cut while the post-cut procedure is unknown. So this round: I confront Mute with my reading in plain terms — one thumb to confirm or reject it — and demand the entire procedure spelled out start to finish in our agreed sign pattern, one step per message, including everything that happens after any cut, adding left/right signs to the language in case positions are needed. To Blind, I send a tactile mapping battery: orientation of the wire row, a confirmable middle wire, and above all any left-right asymmetry anywhere on the face — a screw, seam, panel, bulge — because if one exists that Blind can feel and I can see, our frames lock and I can finally tell Blind which end is wire one. Nobody touches anything; the authorization phrase is still not spoken.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, check my reading of your last message. I understood two statements from it. First: the manual names the target wire by its number, wire one, rather than by the colour word blue. Second, and this is the one that matters: cutting the wire is not the end, because at least one further action is required before the bomb is safe. If I read you correctly, send one message containing a single thumbs up. If I read you wrong, send a single thumbs down and then spell the truth. Then your most important task: spell the complete procedure from the very beginning to the very end, every step in order, one step per message, using only our signs, in this pattern. When a step depends on the light, send the light sign followed by that colour's number: yellow is two, blue is one, red is three. For cutting a wire, send that wire's number followed by the cut sign. For the button, send the fist. For the display, send the display sign plus its number. When the bomb is fully safe and nothing remains, send the open palm. Include everything that happens after any cut, even waiting, even the light or display changing. Two new signs join our language: the leftward hand means left, the rightward hand means right, so spell any position on the bomb with those. One fact per message, nothing else this round. My state check: display still zero, light still yellow, and our blind friend reports the bomb is still completely silent.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind friend, your six answers reached me: three wires, one straight row, same face as the button, no printing or ridges on the wires, complete silence, and the wires feel identical. So we identify your wires by position alone, and I need you to map the face for me. Answer in hand-signs, one answer per message, in this order. Question one: does the wire row run parallel to the button's top edge, thumbs up or down. Question two: can you clearly feel a distinct middle wire exactly between the outer two, thumbs. Question three: explore the whole face slowly and ask whether anything at all makes one end of the wire row feel different from the other end, a screw, a seam, a raised panel, a bulge, a curve, thicker cabling on one side, thumbs up if you find any such difference, thumbs down if the two ends are perfect mirror twins. Question four: where do the wires enter the face, send one finger for the top edge, two fingers for the bottom edge, three fingers for the sides. Question five: is there anywhere on the face a raised plate, dome, or glassy smooth area, such as where the display or light must be, thumbs up or down. Question six: if yes, is that raised or smooth part closer to one end of the wire row than to the other, thumbs up if it leans toward one end, thumbs down if it sits centred. Keep standing facing the button as we agreed. Nothing is cut, nothing is pressed, and my authorization phrase has still not been spoken.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤌", "🤝"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙌 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The procedure is now spelled, not inferred. Decoding Mute: a single 👎 rejects my two-claim reading — so no further action lurks after the cut — followed by the full procedure in our agreed grammar: 🙌 ✌ (light yellow), ☝ 🤏 (cut wire one), ✋ (done, safe, nothing remains — exactly the terminal sign I defined). That matches rounds three and four completely, so the rule is locked from two independent spellings: yellow light → cut wire one, once → finished. The turn-five thumbs-down were evidently answering my round-four questions, not announcing a hidden second step. Blind's map answers cleanly: the row runs parallel to the button's top edge, the middle wire is clearly distinct, the two ends feel like perfect mirror twins, the wires enter from the bottom edge, and the display/light plate sits centred — so there is no bomb-side asymmetry for anchoring. But I don't need one. The geometric insight: Blind stands facing the front face, the same face I read, from the same side — and when two people face the same surface, their left hands point the same way. My visual left is Blind's body left. I can see which end holds wire one, the blue wire: from the front it is the outer wire on the left. So the mapping is simply "the outer wire nearest your left hand as you stand facing the button" — never the middle. I will not authorize on the first pass, though: this round I broadcast the mapping so Mute can veto it by ear, ask Blind to echo back the position in sign (one finger = nearest my left hand, three = nearest my right hand, two = middle), and ask Mute for one final thumb confirming my parse of the procedure spelling. Only when both confirmations arrive green do I speak the authorization phrase next round. State unchanged: display zero, light yellow, silence.

```
speak(text="Blind friend, the complete procedure is confirmed and locked: exactly one cut, and the wire I will have you cut is the outer wire on the side of your left hand as you stand square in front of the button, because you and I are both facing the same face, so my left and your left are the same side. I can see that this wire is the one printed with the number one and the colour I know as blue. The middle wire must never be cut, and neither may the other outer wire. Confirm you have understood me by signing one answer, and nothing else: sign one pointing finger if you understand the target to be the outer wire nearest your left hand, sign three fingers if you believe I mean the outer wire nearest your right hand, sign two fingers if you believe I mean the middle wire. Do not cut anything yet. If your sign matches what I said, I will speak the authorization phrase in my very next turn, and only that phrase, the wire to cut is, followed by the colour, allows you to cut.
```
